attempted_axis: The standing expiry sweep: derive the run-55 CHANGED-UNIT set from git, find every typed denial anchored to a function in those units, RUN each denial's own expiry_check at HEAD, and report EXPIRED or STILL-HOLDS per denial.

attributes.counted_negatives: Two-sided. The POSITIVE side is empty -- zero of seven denials expired -- so the whole value of the sweep is on the negative side, and the negative side has to be shown to be real rather than an unrun check. Each of the four distinct checks was run and each returned a state that FAILS its own expiry trigger by a named register, not by a missing measurement: DoWorldAnimation's ROLE MISMATCH is on 4 webs and the trigger fires below four; ours holds `addi r31,r3,0 @gWorldInfo` where the trigger wants `addi r29,...`; ours puts the two `li 0` in r29/r28 where the trigger wants r31/r30; fn_80051480 loads the seed into f6 where the trigger wants f0. A second negative worth recording: the corpus carries 188 records with a typed denial and only 7 touch a run-55 changed unit, so an expiry sweep scoped to changed units is examining 3.7% of the denial corpus -- cheap, and also a reminder that this sweep says nothing about the other 181.
attributes.law_screen: AGENTS.md's denial contract (a denial must state scope, premise_measurement, expiry_check and falsifier, and the expiry_check is a command a LATER lane can run) is the standard this sweep executes; the sweep is the mechanism that makes a typed denial different from a prose veto. claim.law.CX_an-expiry-check-that-reads-the-postprocessed-object-of-a-pinned-function-can-never-fire.20260904.v2 SCREENED and NOT ENCOUNTERED: none of the seven checks reads a postprocessed object -- two read `--raw` aligned views, one reads savedregs `--raw`, and one reads `fndiff --ops`, all of which read the raw pre-postprocess body or the target, so no check in this set is vacuous. AGENTS.md discipline 8 (remeasure by default) APPLIED and it is what caught the order's changed-unit set. AGENTS.md trap 6c (a filtered grep cannot answer a does-it-exist question) APPLIED: a first grep for denial records hit its 100-file cap, which is a floor and not a total, so the census was redone in-process over every record file. No codegen law applied -- nothing was probed and no source was touched.

attributes.result:
ZERO OF SEVEN DENIALS EXPIRED, AND THE ORDER'S CHANGED-UNIT SET WAS FOUR UNITS TOO WIDE.

THE CHANGED-UNIT SET, CARRIED HERE PER THE NEW RULE. `git diff --name-only 9052e0eda..670e7efac -- src/` (run-54 accept .. run-55 accept) returns exactly three paths:
    src/game/game/gamemain.c
    src/game/pb/pb_error.c
    src/game/sys/ml_mem.c
The same three, and only those three, come back from `git diff --name-only 84f85a96a..670e7efac -- src/` (run-55 stage..accept) and from `git diff --name-only 9052e0eda..e5eb50945 -- src/` (run-54 accept..HEAD), so the set is stable under all three plausible range boundaries. (For completeness, outside src/: config/GUNE5D/splits.txt, config/GUNE5D/webfrank.json, configure.py.) THE WORK ORDER NAMES SEVEN UNITS -- 'mb_camera, critter, ml_mem, gamemain, pb_error, auxanim, enemy'. Four of those did not change in run 55, and each was last touched in run 54 or earlier: `git log --oneline -1 --` gives mb_camera 39128d179 (MBWorldToScreen3D), critter 9add83c16 (CritterCollideWorld), auxanim a19fb90ba (InitOAnimList), enemy cdf25509e (move_logic22), and `git merge-base --is-ancestor <c> 9052e0eda` exits 0 for all four, i.e. every one is an ancestor of the run-54 accept. This is the first run under the rule that the record must CARRY the git command that produced its changed-unit set, and the rule earned itself immediately: executed as written, the sweep would have spent most of its checks on units run 55 never touched.

THE DENIAL CENSUS. 188 records in records/ + inbox/ carry a typed denial (whole-corpus, in-process, no result cap). Joined against the three changed units' rosters read from the built objects (gamemain 74 functions, pb_error 5, ml_mem 26), SEVEN denials touch a changed unit -- four on gamemain::DoWorldAnimation and gamemain::fn_80051480 (two records each), one on gamemain via each pair, and one on pb_error::fn_800C13CC. ml_mem carries none. NOTE ON ml_mem: this is an absence claim and it is measured, not assumed -- no record in the 188 anchors a denial to any of the 26 functions in game/sys/ml_mem, by roster join and by unit-string match.

PER-DENIAL VERDICTS, each against the record's own expiry_check verbatim. (1) attempt.DA_doworldanimation-two-callee-saved-pairs-swap-and-declaration-order-cannot-move-them.20260903.v1 -- check `savedregs ... --raw`, trigger 'if the ROLE MISMATCH list ever drops below four webs, or if r31 ever holds `li 0` in ours'. MEASURED: `ROLE MISMATCH on 4 web(s)` and ours' r31 first definition is `@0x60 addi r31,r3,0 @gWorldInfo`, not `li 0`. STILL HOLDS. (2) attempt.PR_doworldanimation-declared-locals-cannot-outrank-the-address-temps.20260903.v1 and (3) attempt.PR_doworldanimation-the-address-temp-block-is-a-value-kind-not-a-declaration-fact.20260903.v2 -- both carry the identical check `fnasm ... 0x5c:0x95 --raw --diff`, trigger 'if ours ever emits `addi r29,r3,0 @gWorldInfo` at +0x60, or if the two `li 0` at +0x8c/+0x90 ever land in r31/r30'. MEASURED: ours emits `60: addi r31,r3,0 @gWorldInfo(ADDR16_LO)` against the target's `addi r29,r3,0`, and the two `li 0` at +0x8c/+0x90 land in r29/r28 against the target's r31/r30 -- the exact INVERSE of the trigger in both clauses. BOTH STILL HOLD. (4) attempt.PR_fn80051480-the-loop-carried-fpr-accumulator-is-a-second-pointlinedist2d.20260903.v1 and (5) attempt.PR_fn80051480-the-accumulator-is-inserted-at-the-top-of-the-descending-group.20260903.v2 -- identical check `fnasm ... 0x10:0x40 --raw --diff`, trigger 'if ours ever loads the 100000.0f seed into f0 at +0x14'. MEASURED: `14: lfs f6,0(0) @lbl_803468B0(EMB_SDA21)` in ours against the target's `lfs f0`. BOTH STILL HOLD. (6) attempt.DA_fn80051480-the-lever-was-already-applied-and-the-joint-probe-refutes-the-pair.20260903.v3 -- same view, stricter trigger 'if ours ever loads the seed into f0 at +0x14 while the three constants sit in f5/f4/f3'. MEASURED: seed in f6, constants in f4/f3/f2 against the target's f5/f4/f3. STILL HOLDS. (7) attempt.GC_fn800c13cc-the-home-copy-and-the-callee-saved-numbering-are-a-forced-trade.20260904.v1 -- trigger 'if the cluster list is no longer exactly the single `insert T[18:18]@48-48=[] O[18:19]@48-4c=[\'extsh\']` / `delete T[19:20]@4c-50=[\'extsh\']` pair at T51/O51'. MEASURED: `target 51 insns, ours 51`, `opcode multiset: IDENTICAL (51/51)`, and exactly those two clusters and no others. STILL HOLDS.

A TOOL SUBSTITUTION, DECLARED RATHER THAN SILENT. Denial (7)'s expiry_check names `python tools/gdl/probe.py game/pb/pb_error fn_800C13CC --ops`. probe BUILDS, and game/pb/pb_error is an ACTIVE claim of lane WF this run (work_claim.pberror-flip.20260904.v1), as game/game/gamemain is of lane SM (work_claim.split-map-correction.20260904.v1); probe.py and defake_gate.py exit 3 on a foreign claimed unit by design. This sweep therefore ran `fndiff --ops` instead, which reads the object already on disk and prints the same cluster list the check is worded against, with no build and no write. The verdict is unaffected -- the trigger is about the cluster list, which both tools print identically -- but the substitution is recorded because a custodial lane silently swapping a check's named command is exactly the kind of undeclared drift this sweep exists to catch. THE TRANSFERABLE POINT: an expiry_check whose command BUILDS cannot be run by a custodial lane while the unit is claimed, which means a check written as a probe invocation is unrunnable for the whole run on any unit that is in flight. Denials should name a read-only command when one decides the same question.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Four commands, no builds -- re-run the four distinct expiry checks quoted in `result`. Any one of them returning the state its own trigger names refutes this record's zero-expired verdict for that denial, and the denial should then be superseded rather than left standing. The changed-unit half is refuted by `git diff --name-only 9052e0eda..670e7efac -- src/` returning any path this record does not list.
hypothesis.count_consequence: count-neutral: nothing edited, no probe run, no rule authored or deleted. Instruction counts observed while running the checks, quoted as target/ours: DoWorldAnimation 63/63, fn_80051480 58/58, fn_800C13CC 51/51 -- all three at count parity, and none of them moved during this pass.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes -- every check compares against the dtk-split retail objects under build/GUNE5D/obj/**: `fnasm --raw --diff` prints the target stream beside our raw pre-postprocess body, `savedregs` reads both streams, and `fndiff --ops` pairs against the same target. No check reads a postprocessed object, so none of them is vacuous on a pinned function.
hypothesis.statement: EXPIRY CHECKS SHOULD BE WRITTEN AGAINST READ-ONLY TOOLS, AND THE SWEEP SHOULD SAY SO WHEN THEY ARE NOT. Six of the seven checks here name `fnasm`, `savedregs` or `fndiff` and were runnable as written; the seventh names `probe.py`, which builds, and was unrunnable as written because its unit is claimed by another lane this run -- precisely when a custodial sweep is most likely to be looking at it, since claimed units are the ones that just changed. The cheap fix is a convention plus a screen: a denial's expiry_check names a command that performs no build, and a corpus screen flags any expiry_check whose command is probe.py or defake_gate.py. That screen is a grep over the 188 typed denials and belongs to the tool lane. The next expiry sweep should also widen ONE step beyond changed units: the four charter units that did NOT change (mb_camera, critter, auxanim, enemy) are exactly where a stale denial can sit undisturbed for several runs, because nothing about them triggers a changed-unit sweep at all.
